correctness.rationale: For each strictly interior bias the independent binary law is non-atomic and homogeneous self-similar. Conditioning on any finite prefix leaves the same law in affine coordinates, with the limiting biased frequency unchanged. The maps x^2/4 and sqrt(1+x^2)/2 both have positive second derivatives, also after composition with a dyadic affine map. Theorem 3.1 gives a power exponent depending on the original measure only, with map-dependent constants. The inputs and the shifted root therefore have the asserted absolute normality by Fourier normality and translation of the Fourier phase. The unshifted root is half the binary variable; its limiting frequency theta differs from 1/2. Every t in the specified set is non-dyadic, so t and t+1/4 have identical binary tails after position 2 and different root frequencies along the full sequence, which suffices to contradict (TU). The biased-frequency class is Borel and Lebesgue null, and the square map on the relevant compact interval is Lipschitz, proving singularity and nullity. Choose a dyadic cylinder whose closure maps into J. For any 2k sigma>1 the convolution Fourier transform is in L^2, so the convolution is absolutely continuous and gives full mass to the analytic k-fold sumset. The sumset is Lebesgue measurable and positive in measure, so Steinhaus gives a neighborhood in its difference set, not necessarily in the sumset itself.
residual_risks: No explicit optimal decay exponent, sharp convolution order, or interval in the sumset itself is proved.

A single k with 2k sigma>1 works in every cylinder because sigma is a property of the underlying measure. Plancherel and Steinhaus then give exactly the stated positive-measure sumset and neighborhood in the difference set.

originality.rationale: Stephan already gives almost-sure Isaac counterexamples for the identical shifted-square pair and explicitly extends the construction to biased dyadic Bernoulli digits. For that exact family, the additional assertions are direct consequences of Mosquera–Shmerkin's stronger map-uniform nonlinear Fourier decay theorem and its stated normality consequence. On each cylinder one substitutes the two strictly convex compositions into the same theorem on the same measure, and a sufficiently high convolution power then has an L^2 density by Plancherel. Thus lack of an inspected earlier statement of the full conjunction does not establish a distinct scientific claim under the prior-implication standard. This is a finding of prior coverage of the mechanism and its direct consequences, not an assertion that Stephan printed the full conjunction.
residual_risks: The audit does not establish whether the entire conjunction was previously printed verbatim; the failure rests on verified prior implication, not on the bounded search miss.

value.rationale: The motivating question about how large an Isaac counterexample set can be is meaningful. Here the counterexample family and its substantial size were already identified, and the proposed increment is the unrestricted convex-image theorem's routine consequence on exactly that family. The record provides neither a new quantitative bound on k nor a new obstruction or additive phenomenon beyond taking an L^2 convolution power of a Fourier-decaying measure. No distinct valuable remainder is established to repair.
residual_risks: A sharp local decay or sumset assertion would be a different claim and is not adjudicated here.
